notes: Primary contact: Maya Leblanc (CTO). Focus: best-in-class in-editor completions with near-instant feel.
Use-case specifics: multi-cursor completions, inline suggestions as user types, CI-style bulk refactors (batch reranking), context window ~8k tokens.
TTFT targets: aim for 30-50ms median for warm completions; absolute max 100ms for perceived instant UX. Cold-start acceptable up to 120ms but client wants mitigation strategies.
Jitter sensitivity: cadence matters - occasional 80-120ms spikes perceived as stutter. They asked about smoothing strategies (small prefetch tokens, progressive streaming chunks).
Backpressure: when developer types aggressively, client wants graceful degradation (shorter suggestions, partial stream, cancel/replace semantics) rather than timeouts.

Token budget tuning: want per-session and per-file token budgets; dynamic budgets when user requests longer completions (explicit hotkey). Also want telemetry showing tokens spent per suggestion and per-cursor.

Model/version pinning: preference for a stable code-specialized model (gpt-code-3-small). Must support automatic fallback to quantized variant (gpt-code-3-small-q4f) on Dedicated capacity saturations; need rollback SLOs.
Caching: strong interest in prefix/KV cache reuse across small edits. They want cache TTL and explicit invalidation hooks from client-side editor events.
Streaming config: experimenting with 20-30ms emit intervals and 8-16 token chunk sizes. Want Redwood to expose tunable chunk interval and batching latency knobs via Optimize recommendations.
Cost sensitivity: mid-market budget; willing to pay for Dedicated if unit-cost per suggestion predictable. Looking for Optimize suggestions to reduce tokens without harming suggestion quality.
Security/compliance: SSO (Okta), audit logs required for all completions, enterprise KMS integration for key lifecycle. Data residency: US/EU controls for customers in EU.
Quote from CTO on 2025-02-18 call: 'Perceived latency is everything — 50ms feels instant. We will trade token length for consistency.'
POC plan: 2-week perf window. Deliverables: TTFT harness, jitter profile, backpressure policy evaluation, cost per 1k completions estimate.
use_case_summary: Atelier wants to power an IDE copilot with near-instant streaming completions. Key eval metrics: TTFT median, jitter percentiles, backpressure behavior under burst typing, token spending per suggestion, and reliability of model pinning/fallback.
poC_success_criteria: graceful backpressure (no hard errors) under 200 rps of editor events
